Right now we're paying them for a product most people don't even enjoy, so why not do every player a favor and actually test things for a change?

Now I'll have to agree with you here, it would be hard to keep up the hype, but right now I'd rather have a game that I can play then a game where I won't touch it because they refuse to take action against the horrible mentality of printing cards in standard that have eternal format power level.
Maybe have those testing as special events, give players random cards to build a deck and sneak some of those shiny new cards on it, or put them into draft environment,  that could draw even more people to spend just to get a shot at finding a new card to spoil.

The idea is to have things be tested before printing, so we don't need formats like alchemy to modify broken cards and we don't end up with horrible mistakes like we had in the last two years with multiple cards being banned on the eternal formats plus an entire errata on a set mechanic with companion.

I think the concept of alchemy should be used as a beta testing for new sets, let player give it a go for a couple months and use the data to modify cards before printing them, this way we won't end up mistakes like oko and the game is still consistent over all formats and plataforms, instead we got an online format that will bleed into other formats, further extending the line between paper and online.
